Q1(a) [Definition, Classification Tree & Primitive Data Structures]:

[Student Hand-Written Response - Page 1]:
Data Structure: It can be defined as a method of storing and organizing data items in the computer memory.
Mainly deals with:
• Organizing data in memory
• Fetching and processing data
• Storing data in memory

[Classification Tree Diagram]:
Data Structure
  ├── Primitive: int, float, char, double
  └── Non-Primitive:
        ├── Linear: array, stack, queue, linked list
        └── Non-linear: trees, graphs

Primitive Data Structures:
The data structures that are directly operated upon by machine level instructions, i.e., fundamental data types such as int, float, char, double.

[Student Hand-Written Response - Page 2 (Starting at 1b))]:
Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) algorithm is a string-matching algorithm that eliminates backtracking by preprocessing the pattern to construct a prefix/failure function π table.
• Algorithm Logic: On mismatch at character P[q], shift pattern index to π[q-1] to skip redundant comparisons.

Q9(a): Define Graph Data Structure. Explain Graph representations using Adjacency Matrix and Adjacency List with examples and memory comparison.

[Student Hand-Written Response - Page 6]:
A Graph G = (V, E) is a non-linear data structure consisting of vertices V and edges E connecting pairs of vertices.
• Adjacency Matrix: V x V 2D array representation. Fast O(1) edge lookup, but O(V²) space complexity.
• Adjacency List: Array of linked lists representing adjacent vertices. O(V + E) space complexity; efficient for sparse graphs.
• Graph Traversals: BFS uses Queue (level-order traversal); DFS uses Stack / Recursion (path discovery).
